label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The unfinished room retains a narrow, deep entrance-to-rear organization, left framing, and a window on the right portion of the far wall.
Repeated brown timber studs occupy the left wall, but their backing reads as continuous flat panels without individual coursed brick units.
The far-wall window has an inset rectangular assembly, off-white framing, and distinct upper and lower sash regions.
The inclined ladder has paired rails, repeated steps, and a folding top, but its thick pale rails read as painted or plastic rather than aluminum. Rear members visibly disappear into the right wall.
Reverse views clearly show a light rectangular box mounted beside the entrance on the framing, with a connected conduit descending toward the floor.
Many wooden strips form a foreground pile, but masonry debris consists of sparse, regular rectangular chips rather than numerous irregular fragments forming a rubble field.

The floor is mottled and lower rear-wall slats are present, but brick is not recognizable as masonry and the ladder lacks a distinct aluminum appearance. Broad wall surfaces remain overly smooth and uniform.
The delivered view is warmly illuminated but lacks a concentrated high-left work-light emphasis. The bulb and localized pool visible in reverse views do not appear in the authored composition.

The original PNG exists and fully decodes. Its entrance-facing composition shows the rear wall, window, framing, ladder, and foreground debris together and matches the authored-camera rerender. The Blender file opened with separate mesh geometry, assigned node materials, three lights, and an active entrance-side camera.

dimension_scores.evidence: The main room arrangement is recognizable, but missing readable brickwork, sparse rubble, and simplified ladder construction weaken the reconstruction.
Framing and window connections generally read coherently and front ladder feet meet the floor, but rear ladder members disappear into the wall and debris stacking is mechanically simplified.
Brown timber, pale window framing, and warm earth tones fit the subject, but the uniformly beige walls and white ladder lose important color and surface distinctions.
Regular box-shaped chips, clean straight timber, thick cylindrical ladder rails, and visibly noisy rendering give the scene a crude model appearance.
The left framing run, entrance-side electrical fixture, rear-right window, right-side ladder, and foreground wood pile retain the principal spatial relationships.
The corridor proportions are plausible, but walls tower over the window and ladder, while ladder rails are unusually thick relative to its steps and width.
Warm lighting and cast shadows provide depth, but the final view lacks the strong localized work-light effect; masonry and aluminum are poorly differentiated.
The window, framing, ladder, electrical box, utility runs, work lamp, and wood debris are present. Readable exposed brick and a substantial irregular masonry rubble field are missing.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
